newsitem.title: USA: Dow dips as strong dollar clouds large cap outlook.
newsitem.headline: Dow dips as strong dollar clouds large cap outlook.

text.p: U.S. blue chips finished slightly lower on Friday as evidence mounted that a strong dollar was eroding the profit picture for some multinationals.

The Dow industrials fell 15 points to close unofficially at 6805. Eastman Kodak Co tumbled 9-3/4 to 78-1/2 and International Business Machines Corp fell 4-3/8 to 132-1/2 after both shares were hit by currency concerns.
Tobacco shares were also weak, extending their recent slide. Philip Morris Cos Inc fell 4-1/4 to 111-5/8 and Loews Corp slid 5-1/8 to 93-3/8.

Beyond the focused activity in a handful of shares, however, activity was surprisingly muted given the fact that the quarterly "triple witching" expiration of options, index options and index futures took place today.
The quiet tone to the market highlighted a furious sell-off in Kodak, the New York Stock Exchange's most active issue with more than 11 million shares changing hands overall.
Early in the session, the company warned its sales for the first two months of the year were essentially flat versus last year, putting part of the blame on the strong dollar.
Later, two Wall Street firms trimmed their earnings estimates on IBM, again citing the dollar in their actions.
For some time, analysts have cautioned that multinationals would begin to suffer from the strong dollar. With concrete evidence now emerging, they said the concerns could become more widespread.

"Often this starts with somebody signalling to the investment community that there may be a problem," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany. "Then, it starts to become less specific."
"A lot of companies tell us they have adequately hedged for currency swings, but when you see a sophisticated company like Kodak get hit, you start to wonder," he added.
Kodak's sharp fall dragged the Dow to its fourth straight loss, a decline that widened the average's decline to about 131 points for the week.
Broader indicators were generally positive, however. Advancing issues outnumbered declines on the New York Stock Exchange on heavy volume that exceeded 530 million shares.
Tech stocks edged lower, despite holding to positive ground for most of the session.
Analysts continue to watch the group for signs of an end to its sharp two-month retreat, but warned that any recovery would likely take considerable time.

"When a group gets whacked like this and then starts to find a bottom it doesn't typically come roaring back right away," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "There has to be a convalescent period."
Beyond a handful of special situations, the market kept to a measured pace, held in check by next week's Federal Reserve interest rate policy meeting.
Among the special situations, generic drug maker IVAX Corp fell 1-3/4 to 10-5/8 after drug wholesaler Bergen Brunswig Corp called off their merger. Shares in Bergen Brunswig rose 1/8 to 31-5/8.
Outback Steakhouse Inc fell 4-5/8 to 19 after warning its first quarter earnings would not meet Wall Street estimates.

Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp slumped 2-3/4 to 38-1/2 as uncertainty mounted over a federal probe of the company's El Paso, Texas operations. Columbia said it has not been told of the allegations underlying the investigation.
The S&P 500 index rose 1.45 points to 784.10.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.19 points to 1254.07.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
